info.bio: The Trammps fue una de las bandas de disco pioneras salidas de Chicago. Temas como "Zing! Went the Strings of My Heart" (1972) y "Love Epidemic" (1973) fueron todo un bombazo, aunque se les recuerda más por su famoso single "Disco Inferno" (1976), parte de la Banda Sonora de "Fiebre del Sábado Noche". Otros éxitos cosechados incluyen "Bring Back the Night" (1975) y "That's Where the Happy People Go" (1975). En 2005, disco más representativo, "Disco Inferno", entra en el Dance Music Hall of Fame, en Nueva York.

podcast.title: Overwhelming Popularity
podcast.body: The song's immense popularity following the movie led to significant life changes for the band. Jimmy Ellis's daughter, Erica, recounted having to move due to people randomly showing up at their house and being driven to school in a limousine, illustrating the song's widespread cultural impact. "People just started randomly showing up at their house. The next thing she knew, she's being dropped off to school in a limo."

podcast.title: Pioneering "Four on the Floor" Beat
podcast.body: Drummer Earl Young, while working as a session drummer for MFSB at Philadelphia International Records in 1973, developed the iconic "four on the floor" disco sound. He innovated by using his kick drum and hi-hat to create a continuous, driving rhythm for Harold Melvin and the Blue Notes' "The Love I Lost," which became the heartbeat of disco and, by extension, the late 70s. "He used his kick drum and his hi-hat to make the four on the floor sound that really turns out to be the heartbeat of disco and then in many ways, the heartbeat of the late 70s."

podcast.title: Soundtrack Success and Chart Performance
podcast.body: Following its inclusion in the *Saturday Night Fever* soundtrack, "Disco Inferno" soared to number one on the Billboard dance chart for 11 consecutive weeks and reached number 11 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1978. It won a Grammy for Best R&B Vocal by a Group in 1979 and was inducted into the Dance Hall of Fame in 2005. "This time around it made it to number 11 on the Billboard Hot 1778."
